artiest/rick-astley.text:
Rick Astley was born in 1966 in Newton-le-Willows, in the English county of Lancashire. With Never Gonna Give You Up (1987) he made the best-known product of the production trio Stock Aitken Waterman. Twenty years later the song found a second life as an internet joke, which makes Astley an example of how a hit from the 1980s can start circulating again in the digital age.

Astley first drummed in the local soul band FBI and became its singer. Pete Waterman saw him perform in a nightclub in Warrington and brought him to his studio, PWL. There Astley started out as a tea boy and tape operator before he was allowed to sing himself. Never Gonna Give You Up was released in July 1987. Waterman came up with the title and the idea, while Mike Stock and Matt Aitken wrote the melody, chords and lyrics. The bass comes from a Yamaha DX7 synthesizer, the drums from a Linn 9000. Stock said that Trapped (1985) by Colonel Abrams was a major influence. The song spent five weeks at number one in the UK, became the best-selling single of 1987 there and topped the charts in about 25 countries, including the United States. The album Whenever You Need Somebody sold some fifteen million copies worldwide. In 1988 he had another American number one with Together Forever.

In 1993 Astley stopped in order to be with his family. From 2007 his video became the core of rickrolling: a link that promises something else but leads to this clip. In 2021 the video passed a billion views on YouTube. His album 50 (2016) entered at number one in the UK.
artiest/rick-astley.listen: In Never Gonna Give You Up (1987), listen for the jumping bass line from the Yamaha DX7, which Mike Stock built on the model of Trapped by Colonel Abrams. Notice how Astley's deep, mature voice sits on top of it, even though he was only 21 in the video.

artiest/rick-davis.text:
Rick Davis, in full Richard Davis, is an American musician from Detroit, born in 1952. He is regarded as one of the pioneers of techno, as the partner of Juan Atkins in the duo Cybotron. Atkins and Davis began working together in 1981. They made electronic music with synthesizers and drum machines, at a time when that hardly existed in Detroit yet.

In 1981 Cybotron released the single Alleys of Your Mind. Later recordings such as Clear and Techno City followed, and the duo gave its own style the name techno. The music combined the cool sounds of German electronic music with funk and with lyrics about a mechanical future. Davis concentrated mainly on the rougher, more rock-oriented side, while Atkins increasingly wanted to move towards tight electronics. In the end they went their separate ways.

Although Cybotron was active only briefly, it became a model for the young makers around Atkins in Detroit, among them Derrick May and Kevin Saunderson. In the course, Davis is mentioned as the man with whom Atkins started Cybotron in 1981, the beginning of Detroit techno.
artiest/rick-davis.listen: Listen to Alleys of Your Mind by Cybotron and notice the synthesizer lines and the mechanical rhythm. Can you hear how electronics and funk touch each other?

artiest/rick-laird.text:
Rick Laird was an Irish bassist, born on 5 February 1941 in Dublin and died on 4 July 2021. He came from a musical family: his mother played the piano, his father the ukulele. He played those instruments from the age of three. Through his mother he got to know jazz. At sixteen he went to New Zealand with his father and worked on a sheep farm. There he began to take music seriously, at first on guitar.

A record by Oscar Peterson with the bassist Ray Brown made a deep impression on him. He bought a double bass, played along with Brown's records and at eighteen became a professional bassist in Auckland. He played with the pianist Mike Nock and toured New Zealand. At nineteen he went to Sydney for two years, where he played with Don Burrows, among others. In 1962 he moved to England. There he toured with the vocal trio Lambert, Hendricks and Ross, played with Zoot Sims and Al Cohn and did session work. From 1963 to 1964 he studied at the Guildhall School of Music and Drama and played with The Brian Auger Trinity.

He is best known as the bassist and co-founder of the jazz-rock band Mahavishnu Orchestra, with which he performed from 1971 to 1973. That group, led by the guitarist John McLaughlin, brought together jazz, rock and virtuosity. Laird showed that a jazz bassist could also hold his own in the electric music of the 1970s.
artiest/rick-laird.listen: Listen to a Mahavishnu Orchestra recording from the early 1970s and focus on the bass guitar. Can you hear how it gives the guitar and violin playing a solid foundation?

artiest/rick-rubin.text:
Rick Rubin is an American record producer. He was born in 1963 in Long Beach, New York. At secondary school he played in punk bands, and as a film student in New York he had the hardcore band Hose. Through DJ Jazzy Jay of the Zulu Nation he fell under the spell of hip-hop. Together with Russell Simmons he started the label Def Jam in 1984 from his student room. The first release was I Need a Beat by LL Cool J. The Beastie Boys followed, whom he took from punk to rap, and then Public Enemy.

Rubin made hip-hop bare and hard: a heavy drum machine, scratches and often a rock guitar, without much reverb or stacked layers. That worked the other way round as well. In 1986 he produced Walk This Way, on which Run-DMC and Aerosmith remade a rock song together. That record introduced the general public to the combination of rap and hard rock and gave Aerosmith a second life. The same year he made the metal album Reign in Blood with Slayer.

In 1988 he moved to Los Angeles and started a new label, later American Recordings. He produced Blood Sugar Sex Magik (1991) by the Red Hot Chili Peppers, with Give It Away and Under the Bridge, and after that many more albums by that band. From 1994 he made a series of stripped-down albums with Johnny Cash, including a version of Hurt by Nine Inch Nails. Rubin works in virtually every genre and is known for taking artists back to the core of their music.
artiest/rick-rubin.listen: Listen to Walk This Way by Run-DMC and Aerosmith from 1986. Notice how the bare hip-hop beat and the raps combine with Joe Perry's rock guitar and Steven Tyler's voice.

artiest/rick-wakeman.text:
Rick Wakeman is an English keyboard player and composer, born on 18 May 1949 in west London. He wanted to become a concert pianist, but left the Royal College of Music in 1969 and became a sought-after session musician. Of an estimated two thousand sessions, he did several for David Bowie, on Space Oddity and Life on Mars?, for Cat Stevens on Morning Has Broken, and for Elton John, Marc Bolan and Lou Reed. After a short spell with the Strawbs he joined Yes in 1971. There he played on Fragile in 1971, Close to the Edge in 1972 and Tales From Topographic Oceans in 1973.

His own work began with The Six Wives of Henry VIII in 1973, followed by Journey to the Centre of the Earth in 1974 and The Myths and Legends of King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table in 1975. They are concept albums full of progressive rock. In 1974 he formed the English Rock Ensemble, and in 1975 he wrote the music for Ken Russell's film Lisztomania. His discography runs to more than a hundred solo albums, including new age and Christian music, such as Country Airs in 1986 and The Gospels in 1987.

He plays Hammond organ, Moog and Mellotron with technical virtuosity and is known for the capes he wears on stage. In the 1980s and 1990s he also worked for smaller markets, in broadcasting and with a label of his own, and he kept performing, including one-man shows in which he combines music and anecdotes. Wakeman brought the sound of classical music into rock.
artiest/rick-wakeman.listen: Listen to Close to the Edge by Yes and focus on the organ parts and Wakeman's synthesizer. Can you hear how the keyboards are just as important as the guitar?

artiest/ricky-martin.text:
Ricky Martin, in full Enrique Martín Morales, is a Puerto Rican singer and songwriter, born on 24 December 1971 in San Juan. At nine he was already appearing in television commercials, and at twelve he joined the Puerto Rican boy band Menudo. In 1991 he began a solo career with Sony Music Mexico, with the ballads of Ricky Martin in 1991 and Me amarás in 1993, which made him known in Latin America.

His third album, A medio vivir from 1995, took him to Europe. The song María blended Latin styles and became his first international hit. With Vuelve from 1998, which yielded Vuelve and La Copa de la Vida, he won his first Grammy. He sang La Copa de la Vida at the 41st Grammy Awards. In 1999 came his first English-language album, Ricky Martin, with the single Livin' la Vida Loca, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 and the UK chart. Later releases included Almas del silencio in 2003, MTV Unplugged in 2006 and A quien quiera escuchar in 2015, which won a Grammy.

His success in the late 1990s is regarded as the start of the Latin explosion. He is seen as someone who brought Latin pop to the general public and cleared the way for many other Latin American artists. His music combines Latin pop, dance, reggaeton and salsa. He also acted in the soap opera General Hospital and received an Emmy nomination for The Assassination of Gianni Versace.
artiest/ricky-martin.listen: Listen to Livin' la Vida Loca and notice the combination of brass, Latin percussion rhythms and pop singing. Can you hear which instrument carries the rhythm?

artiest/ricky-nelson.text:
Eric Hilliard Nelson, known as Ricky or Rick Nelson, was an American singer and actor, born on 8 May 1940 and died on 31 December 1985. From the age of eight he appeared with his family in the radio and television series The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet. In 1957 he began his career as a singer. His first single was I'm Walkin' with A Teenager's Romance, and the album Ricky reached number one. In 1958 came his first number one, Poor Little Fool, which was also the first number one of the new Billboard Hot 100.

His fame as a television star led to a role in the western Rio Bravo in 1959, alongside John Wayne and Dean Martin. Between 1957 and 1973 he placed 54 songs in the Hot 100, plus seventeen other top-ten hits. When the television series ended in 1966, he became a guest star on other programmes. In his twenties he switched to country rock, after a number of albums of pure country. In 1969 he formed the Stone Canyon Band, and his success returned with the live album In Concert at the Troubadour, 1969, and in 1972 with the hit Garden Party. After that his record label ran into trouble and interest remained limited.

Nelson is one of the first teen idols who became famous through television. He was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame on 21 January 1987. His work shows how the rock 'n' roll of the 1950s blended with country and the television image.
artiest/ricky-nelson.listen: Listen to Poor Little Fool and notice the soft voice and the simple accompaniment. Can you hear how rock 'n' roll sounds almost like a song for quiet listening here?

artiest/rico-rodriguez.text:
Emmanuel Rico Rodriguez, also called Reco or El Reco, was a Cuban-Jamaican ska and reggae trombonist, born on 17 October 1934 in Havana and died on 4 September 2015. As a child he moved with his family to Jamaica and grew up in Kingston. His slightly older schoolmate Don Drummond taught him to play the trombone at the Alpha Boys School. In the 1950s he became a Rastafarian and often performed with the Rasta drummer Count Ossie. He is regarded as one of the first ska musicians.

In 1961 he moved to England, where he played with Georgie Fame's Blue Flames and in reggae bands. With his own band Rico's All Stars and later Rico and the Rudies he recorded the albums Blow Your Horn and Brixton Cat in 1969. In 1976 he made Man from Wareika for Island Records. In the late 1970s he played with the Members on Offshore Banking Business and with the ska revival bands, including The Specials on A Message to You, Rudy. Ian Dury mentions him in Reasons to Be Cheerful, Part 3.

In 1982 he returned to Jamaica to end his career, but in 1987 he toured England again with the Heart Beat Band. Between 1992 and 1995 he played with Jazz Jamaica and Linton Kwesi Johnson, and from 1996 until 2012 with Jools Holland. In 2007 he was appointed a Member of the Order of the British Empire. His trombone links jazz, ska and reggae with the British second wave of ska.
artiest/rico-rodriguez.listen: Listen to A Message to You, Rudy by The Specials and notice the trombone. Can you hear how the brass playing gives the melody a warm, Jamaican sound?

artiest/riem-de-wolff.text:
Riem de Wolff was born in 1943 in Depok on Java and died in 2017 in Blaricum. He was an Indo-Dutch singer and guitarist. In 1949 he came to the Netherlands with his older brother Ruud, where the family settled in Driebergen-Rijsenburg. The two of them grew up there, far from the place where they were born.

Together the brothers formed the duo The Blue Diamonds. Riem sang and played guitar, while Ruud was the other half of the group. In this way a duo with Indo roots emerged in Dutch pop music. The duo went on making records and performing until Ruud's death in December 2000.

Afterwards Riem continued his career alone and went on performing solo. In 2008 he had a part in the Dutch film Ver van Familie, together with, among others, Anneke Grönloh, another singer with Indo roots. In 2005 he was made a knight in the Order of Orange-Nassau. The duo stands for the Indo contribution to Dutch pop history.
artiest/riem-de-wolff.listen: Look up what The Blue Diamonds recorded and listen to the duo's two voices and the guitar. Notice how the brothers make one sound together.

artiest/righeira.text:
Righeira was an Italian Italo disco duo from Turin, consisting of Stefano Righi and Stefano Rota, who called themselves Johnson and Michael Righeira. The two knew each other from secondary school and had been making music together since the late 1970s. As a duo they broke through in 1983 with Vamos a la Playa, a summer hit with a lyric about an atom bomb.

Vamos a la Playa was released in May 1983 on the Italian label CGD. Johnson Righeira wrote it with Carmelo La Bionda, who produced it with his brother Michelangelo. The song is sung in Spanish and built on synthesizers: a simple, skipping melody, an electronic beat and two voices singing the chorus like a beach song. Anyone who follows the lyrics hears about a beach after an atomic explosion. It reached number one in Italy and Switzerland, number two in the Netherlands and Flanders and number three in West Germany. According to La Repubblica, more than three million copies were sold. The duo went on to have more hits with No tengo dinero and L'estate sta finendo (1985), which reached number one in Italy and won the summer competition Festivalbar.

Righeira belongs to Italo disco: dance music from Italian studios, mostly sung in English, with synthesizers and drum machines. Vamos a la Playa is an example of how the fear of the bomb in the 1980s was packaged in cheerful pop music, like 99 Luftballons by Nena. The duo split up in 1992, came back in 1999 and stopped again in 2016.
artiest/righeira.listen: In Vamos a la Playa, listen to how cheerful the synthesizer melody and the sing-along chorus sound, and then pay attention to the lyrics: the 'playa' is a beach after an atomic blast. The contrast between the sunny sound and the content is precisely the trick of the song.

artiest/rihanna.text:
Rihanna, born Robyn Rihanna Fenty in 1988 in Barbados, is a singer and businesswoman. She was discovered on her island in 2003 by the American producer Evan Rogers and signed to Def Jam in 2005, after an audition for Jay-Z and Antonio 'L.A.' Reid. She is an example of the hit factory of the 2000s: an artist who chooses songs from what teams of writers and producers supply.

Her first single, Pon de Replay (2005), brought dancehall from the Caribbean into American R&B and reached number two in the United States and the UK. The real breakthrough came with Umbrella (2007), from the album Good Girl Gone Bad. The song was written by Terius 'The-Dream' Nash, Christopher 'Tricky' Stewart, Kuk Harrell and Jay-Z, and was first offered to Britney Spears. Umbrella spent ten weeks at number one in the UK and seven weeks in the United States, and won a Grammy. Hit after hit followed. Rihanna had fourteen number ones on the Billboard Hot 100 and won nine Grammys.

Besides the music she built a business in fashion and cosmetics. Her brand Fenty Beauty, founded in 2017 together with LVMH, made her a billionaire in 2021, according to Forbes. In 2023 she performed at the Super Bowl halftime show. Rihanna showed how a pop star became a brand in the twenty-first century, with music as one component alongside others, as the Spice Girls had already demonstrated in the 1990s.
artiest/rihanna.listen: In Umbrella, listen to what happens after the chorus: Rihanna chops the word 'umbrella' into pieces ('ella, ella, eh, eh, eh') and turns it into a second hook, the post-chorus. Underneath runs a dry, bare drum loop that stays almost the same throughout the song.

artiest/rinaldo-alessandrini.text:
Rinaldo Alessandrini was born on 25 January 1960 and is a harpsichordist, organist and conductor. He is a virtuoso on Baroque keyboard instruments: harpsichord, fortepiano and organ. His late start is striking. He only began on the piano at around fourteen, while singing in a choir at the same time. At eighteen he discovered the harpsichord. He took lessons with Ton Koopman and gave his first concert shortly afterwards.

Alessandrini is the founder and conductor of Concerto Italiano, an Italian ensemble for early music. The ensemble plays works by Monteverdi, Vivaldi, Couperin and Bach, among others. He is regarded as one of the leading interpreters of early Italian opera. In 2009 he conducted Concerto Italiano at the annual Misteria Paschalia festival in Kraków.

His discography begins in the late 1980s with, among other things, the soundtrack Stradivari: Soundtrack From the Film from 1988 and Fiori Musicali in 1989. In the 1990s came toccatas for harpsichord, suites and partitas and above all many madrigals, including Il sesto libro de madrigali and Quarto Libro dei Madrigali. In this way he contributed to the rediscovery of the Italian Baroque, played on period instruments and in a style that suits the era.
artiest/rinaldo-alessandrini.listen: Listen to a recording by Alessandrini with Concerto Italiano, for example from the madrigal books. Notice how the voices follow one another and how the harpsichord or other continuo carries the rhythm.

artiest/ringo-starr.text:
Ringo Starr, born Richard Starkey in 1940 in Liverpool, is an English drummer, singer and actor. As a child he suffered serious illnesses and long stays in hospital. As a teenager he became fascinated by skiffle. In 1957 he formed his first group, and later he played with Rory Storm and the Hurricanes, a Liverpool band that also performed in Hamburg. In August 1962 he joined the Beatles, replacing Pete Best.

With the Beatles he usually sang one song per album, such as Yellow Submarine and With a Little Help from My Friends. He also wrote and sang Don't Pass Me By and Octopus's Garden. After the group broke up he had solo hits such as It Don't Come Easy, Photograph and You're Sixteen, and in 1973 the successful album Ringo was released. He also acted in films and presented television programmes. Since 1989 he has toured with Ringo Starr and His All-Starr Band.

His drumming style is about feel, not technique. As a result many drummers have come to look at their playing differently: as part of the song. He tuned his drums lower and used damping, which became common much later. In the course, his arrival in 1962 is the moment at which the Beatles' line-up was complete.
artiest/ringo-starr.listen: Listen to Rain by the Beatles and focus on the drums. Can you hear how Ringo lets the rhythm flow and adds small variations without distracting attention from the vocals?

artiest/rinus-gerritsen.text:
Rinus Gerritsen, in full Marinus Gerritsen, is a Dutch bassist, born in 1946 in The Hague. He is best known as a co-founder of Golden Earring. In 1961 he formed a duo with his neighbour George Kooymans. At first it was called The Tornados, but when it turned out that a British group had a hit with Telstar, the name became The Golden Earrings, taken from a song by the British group The Hunters, for whom they had been the support act.

In 1965 the band had a first hit with Please Go, when they were still a pop group with Frans Krassenburg as singer. After two albums Barry Hay became the singer, and around 1970, with the drummer Cesar Zuiderwijk, the line-up was in place that would last fifty years. The group broke through internationally with Radar Love in 1973, followed later by Twilight Zone in 1982 and When the Lady Smiles in 1984. Twenty-five studio albums were released, and the band had almost thirty hits in the Dutch top ten. In 1979 Gerritsen made a solo album with Michel van Dijk and he produced Herman Brood, among others. In 2021 the band announced that its career was over because of Kooymans's illness.

Steve Harris of Iron Maiden cites Gerritsen as an influence on his bass playing. In the course he stands at the beginning of Nederpop: as the man who founded the group that was one of the first from the Netherlands to break through internationally.
artiest/rinus-gerritsen.listen: Listen to Radar Love and focus on the bass, which drives the song along with a rolling pattern. Can you hear how the rhythm sounds almost like a car on the road?

artiest/rita-moreno.text:
Rita Moreno was born in 1931 as Rosa Dolores Alverío Marcano in Humacao in Puerto Rico. At five she moved to New York with her mother. She took dance lessons, as a child voiced Spanish-language versions of American films and at thirteen was already on Broadway. She then signed a contract with MGM, where her first name was shortened to Rita.

In the 1950s she played small parts in film musicals, including Singin' in the Rain in 1952 and The King and I in 1956. Her big breakthrough came in 1961 as Anita in the film version of West Side Story, the musical by Leonard Bernstein and Stephen Sondheim. For it she won an Academy Award for best supporting actress, as the first Latina. She gave the song America a fiercer edge. Even so, the roles after the Oscar often remained stereotyped, which disappointed her.

Moreno also worked in theatre and television. She appeared in The Electric Company, for which she received a Grammy in 1972, and won a Tony in 1975 and Emmys in 1977 and 1978. That makes her one of the few people with an EGOT. In 2021 she returned in Spielberg's new West Side Story, as Valentina and as executive producer.
artiest/rita-moreno.listen: Listen to America from West Side Story and notice how Anita leads the song. Can you hear the fierceness in her voice and the rhythm of the dance?

artiest/rita-moreno-en-george-chakiris.text:
Rita Moreno and George Chakiris are American actors who played the main roles within the Puerto Rican gang, the Sharks, in the 1961 film West Side Story. Moreno played Anita, Chakiris played her boyfriend Bernardo. They are therefore not pop artists in the ordinary sense, but singers and dancers in a film musical. Both received an Oscar for their supporting roles. Their work shows how a Broadway musical went to the silver screen in the 1960s, with music by Leonard Bernstein and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim.

In the song America the world of the Sharks takes centre stage. Anita and the other girls of the group set the praises of life in America against homesickness for Puerto Rico, while the boys contradict them. The piece is built on a Latin American rhythm, with lively dance and singing that goes back and forth like a conversation. Moreno has a career of more than seventy years and was the subject of a documentary in 2021. In this way the film with this song remained, for later generations too, an example of how pop, theatre and dance reinforce one another.
artiest/rita-moreno-en-george-chakiris.listen: Listen to America and notice the rhythm, which feels Latin American, and the conversation between the singers: notice how the girls and the boys contradict one another.

artiest/rita-reys.text: Rita Reys from Rotterdam sang after the war in the orchestra of the drummer Wessel Ilcken, whom she married. In 1956 she recorded The Cool Voice of Rita Reys in New York for Columbia, with, among others, Art Blakey's Jazz Messengers. That was exceptional for a European jazz singer. She was called 'Europe's First Lady of Jazz'. After Ilcken's death she married the pianist Pim Jacobs, with whom she worked for decades, on television as well. She recorded many Brazilian songs and jazz standards. She died in 2013 in Breukelen.
artiest/rita-reys.listen: Listen to the clear, relaxed phrasing, with swing in every line.

artiest/ritchie-blackmore.text:
Ritchie Blackmore, in full Richard Hugh Blackmore, is an English guitarist, born in 1945 in Weston-super-Mare. At eleven he was given a guitar by his father, on condition that he learn to play it properly, and he took a year of classical guitar lessons. Later he took lessons from the session guitarist Big Jim Sullivan. In the 1960s he worked as a studio musician and played in groups such as the Outlaws and with Screaming Lord Sutch.

In 1968 he was a co-founder of Deep Purple. The name came from him: it was his grandmother's favourite song. The first line-up, around the organist Jon Lord, played psychedelic and progressive rock. Later Blackmore also founded Rainbow and Blackmore's Night. His solos are partly classically inspired and partly based on the blues.

Blackmore is known as one of the most influential guitarists, and with Deep Purple he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2016. In the course he appears as the maker of a famous riff, built from two-note chords in fourths. That is the inversion of a fifth, and it gives the riff a solid, open sound.
artiest/ritchie-blackmore.listen: Listen to Smoke on the Water and focus on the riff: two guitar notes at once, always at the same distance. Try singing along to how that riff rises and falls.

artiest/rites-of-spring.text:
Rites of Spring was an American punk band from Washington, D.C., formed in late 1983. The line-up consisted of singer and guitarist Guy Picciotto, guitarist Eddie Janney, bassist Mike Fellows and drummer Brendan Canty. The name refers to the ballet The Rite of Spring by Igor Stravinsky, whose premiere ended in uproar. Picciotto also wanted a rebirth of the local punk scene, which in his view had ground to a halt. In its short existence the band played live only nineteen times and split up in early 1986.

The only album, Rites of Spring, was recorded in February 1985 at Inner Ear Studios and released in June of that year by Dischord Records. Ian MacKaye and Michael Hampton produced it. The band belonged to the Revolution Summer of 1985, a new movement in Washington hardcore. The music is fast and fierce, but also melodic, with more build-up than in ordinary hardcore. What was new lay above all in the lyrics: personal and confessional, about relationships and difficult feelings rather than anger alone.

For that reason Rites of Spring is considered one of the first bands of emo-hardcore, a label the band itself rejected. Picciotto and Canty went on to found the band Fugazi together with Ian MacKaye. Eddie Vedder of Pearl Jam also named Rites of Spring as an influence. Anyone who wants to begin the history of sensitive guitar music ends up here, at a short, intense beginning.
artiest/rites-of-spring.listen: Listen to For Want Of and notice Picciotto's vocals: the voice sounds raw and shouted, but the guitars play a clear melody. Can you hear how the tempo of the song drives forward and at the same time sounds emotional?

artiest/riz-ortolani.text:
Riziero Ortolani, Riz Ortolani for short, was an Italian composer, conductor and orchestrator who wrote mainly film music. He was born in 1926 in Pesaro, the youngest of six children. His father gave him a violin when he was four, and later he switched to the flute. He studied at the conservatoire of his native town and then moved to Rome, where he worked with the RAI orchestra. In the 1950s he played in a well-known Italian jazz band and led dance orchestras abroad.

His big breakthrough came in 1962 with Mondo Cane, a controversial pseudo-documentary. The title song More received a Grammy and an Oscar nomination in 1964. After that Ortolani wrote music for films in England and the United States, such as The Yellow Rolls-Royce, The Spy with a Cold Nose and Buona Sera, Mrs. Campbell. In total he composed for more than two hundred films and television programmes. Many of them were genre films: spaghetti westerns such as Day of Anger, gialli, Euro-spy films and mondo films. Later he often worked for the director Pupi Avati.

His music combines soft, melodic orchestral sounds with jazz and the typical Italian film atmosphere of the 1960s. The songs were also covered outside film, for example by Frank Sinatra and Andy Williams. Music by Ortolani returned in Kill Bill, Drive and Django Unchained. In 2013 he received a lifetime achievement award from the World Soundtrack Academy. He died in 2014 in Rome.
artiest/riz-ortolani.listen: Listen to I giorni dell'ira, the music of the 1967 spaghetti western. Notice how a cinematic melody and a driving rhythm evoke the feeling of a duel.

artiest/rob-hubbard.text:
Rob Hubbard is a British composer who became known in the 1980s for his music for microcomputers, above all the Commodore 64. He began with music as a child, played in bands and worked as a studio musician in the late 1970s. Then he taught himself to program in BASIC and machine code. He chose the Commodore 64 because it had more memory than other machines, and because he had heard that musicians ought to get involved with computers.

Between 1985 and 1989 he wrote or arranged music for more than seventy-five games, as a freelancer and often for British publishers. Well-known pieces include Commando, Monty on the Run, Sanxion, International Karate and Crazy Comets. His favourites included Sanxion and International Karate. In 1988 he moved to Electronic Arts in the United States, where he was the first employee to focus entirely on sound and music. Later he also wrote for the Amiga, the Atari ST and the Mega Drive, including for Populous, Road Rash and Desert Strike.

Hubbard got the very most out of the SID sound chip. His pieces have real melodies, fast arpeggios and an almost orchestral density, despite the limited channels. He even got samples to play by using the chip's volume register. He showed many later makers of chiptune and game music what such a small machine could sound like. His music is nowadays played live by rock bands and orchestras, and in 2016 he received an honorary doctorate from Abertay University.
artiest/rob-hubbard.listen: Listen to Monty on the Run and notice how much is going on at once: a driving melody, an almost danceable bass line and quick ornaments. Remember that all of this comes from a single small sound chip.

artiest/rob-pilatus.text:
Rob Pilatus was born in 1964 or 1965 in Munich and died in 1998. His father was an African-American soldier, his mother a German dancer. He grew up in an orphanage in Bavaria and then with an adoptive family in Munich. As a teenager he worked as a model and breakdancer, and in 1987 he appeared as a backing singer for the group Wind at the Eurovision Song Contest in Brussels, where Wind came second. In 1988 he met Fab Morvan, with whom he briefly formed Empire Bizarre.

The producer Frank Farian discovered them both and turned them into Milli Vanilli. Pilatus and Morvan turned out not to be singing on the records. The voices came from Charles Shaw, John Davis and Brad Howell, while the duo supplied the images with their looks, their hair extensions and their dances. The album Girl You Know It's True became a worldwide hit with three number ones, Girl You Know It's True, Baby Don't Forget My Number and Blame It On The Rain. In 1990 the duo won a Grammy for best new artist.

The fairy tale ended on 15 November 1990, when Farian admitted that the duo had not sung themselves. The Grammy was withdrawn four days later. In 1992 Rob & Fab appeared with their own voices, but that album hardly sold. Pilatus later ran into trouble with the law and drugs and was found dead in a hotel room near Frankfurt in 1998. His story is regarded as the best-known example of lip-syncing in pop history.
artiest/rob-pilatus.listen: Listen to Girl You Know It's True and notice the tight production and the singer's voice. Remember that these are studio singers, not the duo on the cover.

artiest/robbie-van-leeuwen.text:
Robbie van Leeuwen is a Dutch guitarist, sitar player and songwriter, born in 1944. In 1964 he founded The Motions, together with, among others, Rudy Bennett. That was one of the first Nederbeat bands to reach the charts, with a first successful single in 1965.

In 1967 he started Shocking Blue, the group in which the singer Mariska Veres became the face and he was the guitarist and above all the writer. In 1969 the group reached number one with Venus, a song that later also topped the charts in the United States and the United Kingdom and was covered by Bananarama. Love Buzz and Daemon Lover also come from him, and Nirvana released Love Buzz as its first single. In 1974 he left the group and had success with Galaxy-Lin and the single Long Hot Summer. In 1977 he started the group Mistral together with Rick van der Linden, which worked mainly with synthesizers. After that he withdrew from the music world. In 2013 he received the Buma Lifetime Achievement Award.

Van Leeuwen wrote songs with a clear, sharp melody and a strong guitar theme, and showed that a Dutch band could score worldwide. In the course he appears as the brains behind Shocking Blue.
artiest/robbie-van-leeuwen.listen: Listen to Venus and notice the guitar riff at the beginning, the sitar and the low, powerful voice of Mariska Veres. Which sound lingers the longest?

artiest/robert-craft.text:
Robert Craft was born in 1923 in Kingston in the state of New York and died in 2015 in Florida at the age of 92. He was a conductor and writer and studied at the Juilliard School. He was captivated early on by early music by Monteverdi, Gesualdo and Schütz and by the modern composers of the Second Viennese School.

His life changed in 1948, when he met Igor Stravinsky. Until the composer's death in 1971 he worked with him, first as an assistant, later as an artistic partner. He lived with Igor and Vera Stravinsky in Hollywood and later in New York. Together they produced a series of books, including Conversations with Igor Stravinsky in 1959, full of conversations, essays and diary fragments. Craft also conducted the world premieres of Stravinsky's late works in twelve-tone technique, such as Agon, The Flood and Requiem Canticles.

As a conductor Craft led the major American orchestras and performed in Europe, Russia, Japan and on other continents. He was the first American to conduct Alban Berg's Wozzeck and Lulu. In the mid-1950s he recorded the complete works of Anton Webern. His recordings of Stravinsky with the Orchestra of St. Luke's and his recordings of Varèse earned him, among other honours, the Grand Prix du Disque and the Edison Prize. In 2002 his autobiography An Improbable Life appeared.
artiest/robert-craft.listen: Listen to a recording of Stravinsky's Agon conducted by Craft. Notice the clear, bare sounds of the orchestra and the rhythms that keep shifting.

artiest/robert-fripp.text:
Robert Fripp is an English guitarist, composer, producer and writer, born in 1946 in Wimborne Minster in Dorset. He was given a guitar at the age of eleven and knew, as he said later, almost at once that this would be his life. He played rock 'n' roll, traditional jazz and modern jazz, and listened to music by Bartók and the Beatles. After secondary school he played in dance bands in Bournemouth, where he met musicians he would later work with, such as John Wetton and Greg Lake.

Fripp is best known as the guitarist, founder and only constant member of the progressive rock band King Crimson. He also worked as a session musician and collaborator with, among others, David Bowie, Blondie, Brian Eno, Peter Gabriel, Talking Heads and David Sylvian. His name appears on more than seven hundred releases. He devised a tape-delay system called Frippertronics, later replaced by the digital Soundscapes, and used a tuning of his own, the New Standard Tuning. His compositions often have unusual, asymmetrical rhythms.

Fripp showed that a guitar need not only play riffs and fast solos, but can also make long, floating sounds. In the magazine on rock behind the Iron Curtain he therefore appears as a listening tip: a long, shrieking note that never seems to stop.
artiest/robert-fripp.listen: Listen to Fripp's guitar and notice the long, sustained note that floats above the rest. Can you hear how the sound is almost like a synthesizer, and yet comes from a guitar?

artiest/robert-glasper.text: The pianist Robert Glasper from Houston studied in New York and played both in jazz groups and with hip-hop and R&B artists. He names Herbie Hancock and the producer J Dilla as major influences. With the Robert Glasper Experiment he made Black Radio in 2012, with guest singers such as Erykah Badu, Lalah Hathaway and Yasiin Bey. The album won the Grammy for best R&B album. Glasper played on To Pimp a Butterfly by Kendrick Lamar. He shows that jazz, hip-hop and soul are one musical language for his generation.
artiest/robert-glasper.listen: Hear how the piano and the beat take turns beneath the vocals.

artiest/robert-glasper-experiment.text:
The Robert Glasper Experiment is the electric group of the pianist Robert Glasper, who was born in 1978 and comes from Texas. Glasper began as a jazz pianist in church, where he learned to blend gospel harmony and jazz harmony. At the New School in New York he met the neo-soul singer Bilal. That led to a second career alongside jazz, between hip-hop and R&B. Glasper became, among other things, the musical director of Yasiin Bey, formerly Mos Def.

The Experiment first appeared in 2009 on the album Double-Booked, on which Glasper plays both with an acoustic trio and with his electric band. It featured Derrick Hodge on bass, Casey Benjamin on saxophone and vocoder and Chris Dave on drums. Later Mark Colenburg took over on drums. The breakthrough album Black Radio was released in 2012, with guests such as Lupe Fiasco, Bilal, Lalah Hathaway, Erykah Badu and Yasiin Bey. In 2013 it won the Grammy for best R&B album. Black Radio 2 followed in 2013, and in 2016 ArtScience, the first Experiment album without guest singers, on which all the members wrote and produced.

The group makes jazz that sounds like contemporary soul and hip-hop: loose rhythms, electric keyboards, the vocoder and room for improvisation. In doing so it built a bridge between the jazz audience and a younger audience and showed that jazz can sound like the music on the radio.
artiest/robert-glasper-experiment.listen: Listen to a track from Black Radio and notice the drums and the electric piano. Can you hear where the jazz is and where the hip-hop begins?

artiest/robert-henke.text:
Robert Henke was born in 1969 in Munich and lives in Berlin. He is a German artist who works with computers: he makes music, installations with image and light, and live performances. His background lies in technology. He builds his own instruments and algorithms and finds technical objects beautiful. His material consists of generated sound and image, field recordings, photographs and light. It is processed with mathematical rules, interaction and controlled chance. In recent years he has also worked with powerful lasers.

Together with Gerhard Behles he created the music software Ableton Live, a program that has been used in many studios and on many stages. In 1995 he started the project Monolake with Behles, under which he makes electronic music. Albums such as Hongkong (1997), Interstate (1998), Gravity (2000) and Cinemascope (2001) belong to it. Under his own name there appeared, among others, Piercing Music in 1994, Floating.Point in 1997, Signal to Noise in 2004 and Layering Buddha in 2006. In 2024 he composed the soundtrack for the Netflix series CROOKS.

Henke also teaches and gives lectures on sound and computers, including at the Universität der Künste in Berlin and at Stanford. His installations have been shown at, among other places, Tate Modern and the Centre Pompidou. In this way he combines pop, technology and visual art.
artiest/robert-henke.listen: Listen to a track by Monolake and notice the sounds: is the music built from rhythm, noise or repetition? Try to hear what in the track seems to be a machine at work.

artiest/robert-johnson.text:
Robert Johnson was an American blues musician from the Mississippi Delta, probably born in May 1911 in Hazlehurst. He travelled through the South as a singer and guitarist and played on the street, in juke joints and at parties. He has become the best-known Delta blues musician, above all thanks to the rock musicians who discovered him in the 1960s.

Johnson recorded a total of 29 songs in San Antonio in November 1936 and in Dallas in June 1937, with the producer Don Law. He played alone, on an acoustic guitar, often with a bottleneck or slide and in an open tuning. His guitar plays a bass line, a rhythm and melody lines that answer the voice, all at the same time. He recorded Cross Road Blues on 27 November 1936 at the Gunter Hotel in San Antonio. It was released in 1937 as a 78 rpm record on Vocalion. The song is about a man who kneels at a crossroads and cannot get a ride as evening falls. Johnson died in August 1938 near Greenwood, aged 27, of a cause that has never been established.

The story that he sold his soul to the devil at a crossroads actually belongs to another bluesman, Tommy Johnson. It was later pinned on Robert. In 1961 Columbia released the compilation King of the Delta Blues Singers. That record found its way to British and American rock musicians. The Rolling Stones recorded Love in Vain, Led Zeppelin Traveling Riverside Blues, and Cream played Crossroads (1968) with Eric Clapton. In 1986 Johnson was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as an early influence.
artiest/robert-johnson.listen: In Cross Road Blues, listen to the slide guitar: Johnson slides a bottleneck across the strings, so that the notes glide and wail like a second voice. Try counting the bars too: he stretches a line or moves on early, because he follows the lyrics and not a fixed twelve-bar scheme.

artiest/robert-king.text:
Robert King was born in 1960 in Wombourne, England. He is a conductor, harpsichordist, organist, music publisher and writer. As a boy he sang in the choir of St John's College, Cambridge, where he studied music from 1979 to 1982. In 1980 he won the Brian Runnett Organ Prize there.

In that same year he founded The King's Consort, an orchestra that plays on period instruments. He is its conductor and artistic director and made more than a hundred recordings with the ensemble, mainly for Hyperion Records, between 1987 and 2007. Since 2012 he has recorded for the label Vivat, with I Was Glad as his first album, which reached number one in the UK classical chart. His recordings of Purcell were repeatedly finalists for the Gramophone Awards.

His repertoire lies mainly in the Baroque, with Purcell as its centre of gravity. He also conducts Mozart, Haydn and Mendelssohn and English composers of the early twentieth century such as Vaughan Williams, Stanford and Parry. He has worked with orchestras and choirs in Europe and North America, wrote a book on Purcell in 1995 and published many scores. In the 1990s he also sat on the board of a British organisation that ensured musicians are paid when their work is broadcast.
artiest/robert-king.listen: Listen to a recording by The King's Consort, for example of Purcell. Notice the sound of the old instruments and how the choir and the orchestra follow one another.

artiest/robert-miles.text:
Robert Miles was the pseudonym of Roberto Concina, born in 1969 in Fleurier in Switzerland to Italian parents. He grew up in Fagagna in Friuli, Italy, played the piano and worked as a DJ in clubs and on radio stations. In 1990 he started a studio of his own and a pirate station with his savings. He chose the name Robert Miles to suit the international musical journey he had in mind.

In 1994 he wrote Children, a calm piece that began as trance and chill-out on acoustic guitar chords and soft synthesizer sounds, and later acquired a piano theme. The song came out in 1995 and within two weeks became a success all over Europe. It topped the charts in many countries. According to the story, he wanted to calm dancers at raves before they drove home. The debut album Dreamland appeared in 1996, with, among others, Fable and a cover of One and One with the singer Maria Nayler. In 1997 came 23am, with Freedom and vocals by Kathy Sledge. After that he set up his own label Salt Records and made Organik, Miles_Gurtu with the percussionist Trilok Gurtu, and Th1rt3en.

Miles developed dream trance: melodic, soft and cinematic, with the piano sound as its signature. Later he sought influences from trip-hop, Indian music, jazz and rock. He died in 2017 in Ibiza at the age of 47. His work shows that dance music could also be calm and reflective.
artiest/robert-miles.listen: Listen to Children and notice the piano melody that keeps returning, above a calm, even beat. Notice how slowly the song builds and how calm it stays, even though it is dance music.

artiest/robert-plant.text:
Robert Plant was born in 1948 in West Bromwich and grew up in the Black Country in the English Midlands. He began training as an accountant, but quickly gave it up. At sixteen he left home to sing in local blues bands, including Band of Joy with the drummer John Bonham. In 1968 the manager Peter Grant and the guitarist Jimmy Page asked him to join the Yardbirds. With him that group turned into Led Zeppelin, of which he was the singer and lyricist until it broke up in 1980.

Plant was a charismatic frontman with a raw, powerful voice with a wide range. His blues influences could be heard in Led Zeppelin. After 1980 he carried on solo with Pictures at Eleven in 1982 and The Principle of Moments in 1983, both in the American top ten. With the Honeydrippers he had a hit in 1984 with Sea of Love, a cover of a 1959 song on which Page played. Now and Zen from 1988 is his best-selling solo album. In the 1990s he worked with Page again, which earned a Grammy in 1998 for Most High.

Later he kept choosing different paths, including with Strange Sensation, the album Mighty ReArranger in 2005 and Raising Sand in 2007 with Alison Krauss. That album won the Grammy for album of the year in 2009. Led Zeppelin entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1995. Plant is regarded as one of the great rock singers and as the model for the hard rock vocalist.
artiest/robert-plant.listen: Listen to a Led Zeppelin song with Plant, for example Whole Lotta Love, and notice how his voice pushes against Page's guitar. Can you hear the blues in his phrasing?

artiest/robert-schumann.text:
Robert Schumann was a German composer, pianist and music critic of the early Romantic period. He was born in 1810 in Zwickau, into a prosperous family in which his father was a bookseller and publisher. For him music and literature always went together, with writers such as Jean Paul as favourites. He first studied law in Leipzig and Heidelberg, but in the end chose music and took piano lessons with Friedrich Wieck. His dream of a career as a virtuoso foundered on a lingering problem with his right hand, and so he turned to composing.

His early work is almost entirely for piano, with pieces that often suggest a story or an image: Carnaval, Davidsbündlertänze, Fantasiestücke and in 1838 Kinderszenen, which contains Träumerei. In 1840 he married Wieck's daughter Clara, against Wieck's wishes. In the years that followed he wrote many songs and song cycles, such as Frauenliebe und Leben and Dichterliebe. From 1841 came four symphonies and chamber music, including a piano quintet. In 1850 he moved to Düsseldorf as music director, but his insecurity and his unstable health made the work difficult. In 1853 he met the young Johannes Brahms. A year later he was admitted to an asylum near Bonn, where he died in 1856.

Schumann's is dreamy, personal music, full of shifting moods and short, songlike themes. His piano music and his songs are the basis of his fame. He became a model for later composers such as Mahler, Strauss and Schoenberg, and for the French.
artiest/robert-schumann.listen: Listen to Träumerei from Kinderszenen and notice the simple, songlike melody. Follow how the pianist lets the tempo breathe and lets the phrases end like a softly spoken thought.

artiest/robert-smith.text:
Robert Smith is an English singer and guitarist, born in 1959 in Blackpool and raised in Crawley. As a child he had piano lessons and later guitar lessons, but mostly taught himself to play by listening to his brother's records. In 1976 he founded the post-punk band The Cure, of which he became the singer, guitarist and main writer. He is the only member who has always stayed. From 1982 to 1984 he also played guitar with Siouxsie and the Banshees, and in 1983 he briefly started the project The Glove.

The 1980 album Seventeen Seconds contains the song A Forest. His guitar playing, in which he uses the Fender Bass VI among other instruments, and his own high voice form the sound of The Cure. His appearance is part of it too: pale skin, red lipstick, black eyeliner, tousled black hair and black clothes. That image had a strong influence on the goth culture of the 1980s.

Smith showed that pop music can be dark and sensitive without losing its catchiness. In 2019 The Cure was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. In the course he is the singer of the band that shows with A Forest how cool and bare rock could sound in the early 1980s.
artiest/robert-smith.listen: Listen to A Forest and notice the bass and the guitar line, which circle around each other. How do the space between the notes and the thin voice make the song tense?

artiest/robert-westerholt.text:
Robert Westerholt was born in 1975 in Waddinxveen. He is a guitarist and co-founder of Within Temptation, a Dutch symphonic metal band. At secondary school he got to know Sharon den Adel, Jeroen van Veen and Martijn Spierenburg. In 1992 he started the band The Circle with Spierenburg and Van Veen and wrote his first music of his own. A demo from December 1992 was given the title Symphony No. 1. The group later continued as Voyage, and Den Adel took part in a CD.

When Voyage came to an end, Westerholt started a new project with his girlfriend Sharon den Adel. He sent demos of Enter and Candles to Van Veen, who joined him. In 1997 the line-up was complete, and that same year Within Temptation signed with DSFA Records and the debut album Enter was released. Westerholt writes the music and on the first albums, Enter and The Dance, sings part of the vocals in the form of grunting, the raw singing that belongs to metal. That combination of his growl with Den Adel's clear voice marked the band's beginnings.

In 1998 he had a small part as Death in Ayreon's rock opera Into the Electric Castle. Since 2011 he no longer tours with the band, because he is looking after his children. He remains a member for recordings and concentrates on songwriting and production. Stefan Helleblad replaces him live. In 2018 he married Den Adel.
artiest/robert-westerholt.listen: Listen to an early Within Temptation song, for example from the album Enter. Notice the interplay between the guitars, the symphonic keyboards and Sharon den Adel's voice.

artiest/robin-s.text:
Robin S. is the stage name of Robin Stone, an American singer, born in 1962 in Queens, New York. She worked as a house singer and became best known for Show Me Love. The first version of that song appeared in 1990 and was produced by Fred McFarlane. At the time it was only a modest success.

In 1993 the Swedish DJ and producer StoneBridge made a remix, and Big Beat Records re-released that recording under the name Robin S. This time it did become a big hit, which also reached number one in the American dance clubs. The 1993 album Show Me Love was largely produced by StoneBridge. Luv 4 Luv was the follow-up. Her second album From Now On appeared in 1997 on Atlantic Records, with Todd Terry and Eric Miller among the producers. It went beyond dance music and also contained gospel and R&B ballads. The single It Must Be Love was again a hit in the clubs.

In Europe her music always found a larger audience than at home. She performed during a European tour in 2004 and became a regular guest at parties built around the music of the 1990s. In October 2008 the radio mix of Show Me Love reached the top of the Dutch Top 40, her most successful song in the Netherlands. In 2016 she was back at the top of the American dance chart with Shout It Loud, together with the DJ Escape.
artiest/robin-s.listen: Listen to Show Me Love and notice the piano and the bass drum that carry the song. Can you hear how her voice rises above the dance floor?

artiest/robin-thicke.text:
Robin Thicke was born in 1977 in Los Angeles. His mother is the actress and singer Gloria Loring, his father was the actor Alan Thicke. His parents also wrote television theme music. Robin wrote songs of his own at an early age and formed a vocal group while still young. A demo, paid for by the jazz singer Al Jarreau, ended up with the R&B singer Brian McKnight, who helped him find work as a writer and producer. At seventeen he was living on his own and making a living by writing and producing for others, including Brandy, Color Me Badd, Brownstone and Christina Aguilera.

As an artist he signed with Interscope, but his 2002 debut A Beautiful World was not a commercial success. In 2005 he joined Pharrell Williams's label Star Trak for The Evolution of Robin Thicke. Next came Something Else in 2008, with the hit Magic, Sex Therapy: The Session in 2009 and Love After War in 2011. His style is blue-eyed soul: R&B with a smooth, soft falsetto voice.

His biggest hit came in 2013 with Blurred Lines, with T.I. and Pharrell Williams. The song received Grammy nominations and topped the American chart. The album of the same name reached number one in the United States and the United Kingdom. Since 2019 he has also been a panellist on the television programme The Masked Singer.
artiest/robin-thicke.listen: Listen to Blurred Lines and notice the groove, Thicke's falsetto and the role of Pharrell Williams and T.I. in the song.

artiest/rocafil-jazz.text:
Rocafil Jazz was the band of Prince Nico Mbarga, a highlife musician who was born in 1950 to a Cameroonian father and a Nigerian mother. As a boy Mbarga learned the xylophone from his father and built one himself. During the Nigerian civil war he fled to Mamfe in Cameroon, where he worked as a band boy for a Congolese group. There he got to know Congolese rumba and taught himself conga, bass and electric guitar.

After the war he founded Rocafil Jazz, which got regular gigs at the Plaza Hotel in Onitsha. After a disappointing single in 1973 came the first success with I No Go Marry My Papa. EMI then dropped the band. It then signed with Rogers All Stars, a Nigerian label in Onitsha, and recorded Sweet Mother. That song from 1976 is sung in Pidgin and became one of the best-selling records in Nigerian music history. Between 1975 and 1981 the band made nine albums for that label.

The music blends Nigerian and Congolese guitar playing with cheerful highlife rhythms and Mbarga's soft singing. In this way it was important for the development of African pop music. Sweet Mother is sometimes called Africa's anthem and was chosen by BBC listeners as their favourite African song. After quarrels the original band fell apart, and Mbarga died in 1997.
artiest/rocafil-jazz.listen: Listen to Sweet Mother and notice the light guitar lines and the rhythm. Can you hear how the singing in Pidgin seems to talk to the audience?

artiest/rock-steady-crew.text:
The Rock Steady Crew is a group of breakdancers from New York. In 1977 the b-boys Jimmy Dee and Jimmy Lee started the group in the Bronx, the borough where hip-hop emerged in those years. Breakdance, or breaking, was the dance element of hip-hop culture there, alongside rap, DJing and graffiti. In 1979 Crazy Legs and B-Boy Fresh started a chapter in Manhattan. Crazy Legs became the group's best-known face. The New York Times later called the Rock Steady Crew the most important breakdance group in the world.

In the early 1980s the dancers ended up in films, such as Flashdance and Beat Street. As a result young people outside New York saw for the first time how b-boys showed off their skills on the street, with spinning moves on the floor and on their heads. In 1983 the group even got a hit of its own: (Hey You) The Rock Steady Crew, from the album Ready for Battle. The song was a top ten hit in Great Britain and in many other European countries. It was electronic dance music with a cheerful chorus, made for dancing.

The Rock Steady Crew grew into a kind of brand, with groups in other places. DJs and rappers such as DJ Qbert and Rahzel also belonged to it. In the 1980s the crew helped spread hip-hop culture all over the world.
artiest/rock-steady-crew.listen: Listen to (Hey You) The Rock Steady Crew from 1983. Notice the electronic beat and the chorus that shouts the name of the group, and imagine how breakdancers moved to it.
